chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from al-Hasan ibn Hammad ibn 'Udayn, from 'Imran ibn Humran, who said:

I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him): 'Should I shorten the prayer in the Sacred Mosque (Mecca) or complete it?' He said, 'If you shorten it, it is permissible; if you complete it, it is better, and adding to the good is good.' It is also recommended to complete the prayer in the sanctuary of Kufa and al-Ha'ir, for their residents, with the peace (of God) added to these two sanctuaries, as narrated.
ai.seo_question: Should I shorten or complete my prayer in Mecca's Masjid al-Haram?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) clarifies the juristic preference for completing the four-rak'ah prayer in Masjid al-Haram, establishing it as 'excess goodness' rather than a mandatory obligation. The hadith further extends this recommendation to the sanctuaries of Kufa and al-Ha'ir for their respective residents, reflecting the Shia scholarly tradition of treating these sites with the same reverence as the Sacred Mosque. This ruling underscores the principle that while shortening is permissible, performing the full prayer in these holy precincts yields greater spiritual reward.
